title: 10 Optmyzr alternatives for PPC and conversion tracking
summary: Compare Optmyzr alternatives for PPC teams: bid tools, audit platforms, and conversion tracking checks. Trade-offs, ideal users and selection criteria.
body_markdown:
Pick the tool by the job, not the feature list. Teams searching for Optmyzr alternatives usually want fewer hours inside the ad account, and the tool that delivers that depends on the job.


Before you switch, name the job. Bid rules. Account audits. Budget pacing. Cross-channel reporting. Or the conversion data those systems learn from. A bidding tool that trains on duplicate purchases will optimize the wrong thing, however clean its rules look. In a 2025 survey of 200 CMOs across the United States, United Kingdom, Germany, Austria and Switzerland, **45% of the marketing data chief marketing officers used for business decisions was considered incomplete or inaccurate** . Automation does not wait for you to notice.


The ten options below are grouped by job. Each entry says what the tool does, who it suits, and where it stops. Some edit campaigns. Some only watch them. One checks the hits underneath both.


Match the tool to the failure you have. If search terms are a mess, an audit tool can pay for itself in a week. If Meta and GA4 purchase counts disagree, no bid rule fixes that. The same discipline applies outside paid media: a technical[seo audit ireland](https://baikou.agency/seo/audit/) teams can act on beats a longer report nobody reads.


## 1. Trackingplan


Trackingplan


Start here if your problem is the number, not the bid. Trackingplan is an analytics agent for paid media teams, analysts, agencies and privacy leads. It reads requests sent to **more than 170 analytics and ad providers** from websites, apps and server-side endpoints, plus the dataLayer, and verifies every event, property and value on real traffic.


For paid media it surfaces the failures that break automation: missing or duplicate conversions, value mismatches, click-ID and match-rate gaps, broken UTMs and campaign naming. Meta is the clearest case.[Meta's Conversions API best practices](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/ads-commerce/conversions-api/best-practices/) require overlapping browser and server events to share the same event name and a deduplication key, either an identical **event_id** or a combination of` external_id` and` fbp` , point to the Test Events tool to see which events were deduplicated, and score **Event Match Quality out of 10** . A purchase sent twice through the Meta Pixel and CAPI, or a server hit with thin identity parameters, changes what Advantage+ learns from.


### What it does with a finding


Every finding links to the underlying hits, so an analyst can trace a bad purchase to a tag, a trigger, a release or a dataLayer change instead of guessing. Results route to Slack, Teams, email or a webhook. You describe a report, an audit or a recurring check in plain English, and scheduled automations run **daily or weekly** . Consent and PII monitoring covers websites and server-side implementations.


It makes sure campaigns are optimized on conversion data the team can trust, and it starts with a **9-day free trial** .[Elogia](https://www.trackingplan.com/customer-stories/how-elogia-scaled-value-with-trackingplan) and[Havas Media Network](https://www.trackingplan.com/customer-stories/how-csa-havas-media-network-regained-client-trust-with-out-of-the-box-data-quality-monitoring) tell how they use it.


## 2. Adalysis


Adalysis


[Adalysis](https://adalysis.com/) is the pick when your accounts drift. It runs ongoing audits across Google Ads and Microsoft Advertising, with **more than 100 automated account audit checks** , customizable alerts, ad testing and experiment analysis, and bulk optimization and reporting.


The value is repetition. Missing ads, keyword conflicts, disapproved creatives and neglected ad groups get flagged every cycle rather than once a quarter when someone remembers. Unlimited linked accounts and users are included across plans, which matters for agencies. Pricing is based on monthly ad spend, and a **30-day free trial** is available.


One audit item deserves manual attention.[Google's conversion action guidance](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/16563287) states that primary conversion actions are eligible for bidding while secondary actions are observation-only, and that a significant change in the conversion behavior used for bidding may need **one to two conversion cycles** for the system to adapt. An account can pass every structural check and still feed Smart Bidding the wrong action.


- **Best for:** search-first teams that want account health checks and test analysis.
- **Stops at:** paid social. There's no broad social management here.
- **Costs:** spend-based paid plans, no free plan listed.


If you're building a repeatable checklist rather than buying software, our[Google Ads audit tool walkthrough](https://www.trackingplan.com/blog/google-ads-audit-tool) covers the checks worth running by hand first, and the[PPC audit tools comparison](https://www.trackingplan.com/blog/best-ppc-audit-tools) puts Adalysis, TrueClicks and Opteo side by side as audit tools.


## 3. TrueClicks


TrueClicks


Say an agency runs twelve search accounts and one client overspends by mid-month.[TrueClicks](https://www.trueclicks.com/) is built for that week. It combines PPC audits with prioritized recommendations, performance alerts in Slack and Teams, KPI tracking against CPA and ROAS targets, and budget pacing across Google Ads and Microsoft Ads, plus Meta budget monitoring.


The free plan covers up to **$50,000 in monthly ad spend** , which makes it easy to test on a real portfolio before committing. Above that tier, paid pricing scales with spend.


Where it stops is measurement. Pacing and KPI alerts read the conversions the platform reports.[Google's own documentation on reporting differences](https://support.google.com/analytics/answer/13965727) explains that key events and Google Ads conversions can report different numbers because of the attribution model, the conversion window, the counting method and identity settings.


So treat a TrueClicks alert as a prompt to compare event definitions, counting rules, attribution windows and imported conversions. It isn't a full campaign-management suite across social platforms, and thresholds need account context. Set them per client, not globally, or you'll mute the alerts by week two.


## 4. Opteo


Opteo


[Opteo](https://opteo.com/) suits the solo manager who wants a short list of fixes, not a platform. It's built around Google Ads, with integrations for Microsoft, Meta, LinkedIn and TikTok Ads: recommendations, account monitoring, reporting, ad preview and sharing, with connections for individual accounts and manager accounts. Published tiers make the cost easy to estimate, and a free trial is available.


The trade-offs are structural. Account and spend caps constrain larger agencies. Published refresh cycles are **24 or 12 hours depending on tier** , not continuous, so a tracking break at 9am may not surface until the next day.


There's also a prerequisite most comparison pages skip.[One Optmyzr alternative review](https://scaleyai.com/blog/optmyzr-alternative) states plainly that conversion tracking must already be working before the tool can be useful, and frames Smart Bidding as effective only when tracking is clean and conversion history is sufficient. A recommendation engine inherits that assumption. It'll suggest bid moves based on whatever conversion count the account reports.


- **Choose it when:** one person owns Google Ads and wants guided improvements.
- **Pair it with:** a post-release check on purchase and lead hits.


I'd rather see a small team run Opteo plus a tracking check than a large suite nobody configures properly.


## 5. Adpulse


Adpulse


Budget control across networks is a different job from search auditing.[Adpulse](https://adpulse.app/) does cross-platform pacing and allocation, a portfolio dashboard with performance alerts, and search-term and shopping analysis. Platform coverage includes Google, Meta, Microsoft, TikTok, LinkedIn, Pinterest, Reddit, Amazon Ads and ChatGPT. Published plans and a **14-day trial** let you test the workflows before rollout.


Breadth brings a data problem.[IAB's State of Data 2024](https://www.iab.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/IAB-State-of-Data-2024.pdf) identifies declining data quality and accuracy as a direct threat to attribution, ROI measurement, conversion tracking and campaign optimization, and describes brands, agencies and publishers adopting first-party data and enrichment tools to compensate for lost observability.


### What to verify before you allocate


A portfolio view is only as good as the channel grouping behind it. Check that UTM values, campaign naming, click IDs such as GCLID and FBCLID, and event timestamps line up across networks. If naming is inconsistent, the unified dashboard splits one channel into three and your allocation logic follows the split.


Pricing rises with ad spend, and Google-only advertisers won't need most of this. For teams comparing the reporting side of the category, our[SEM reporting tools comparison](https://www.trackingplan.com/blog/sem-reporting-tools) separates dashboard breadth from data lineage. Verify each channel integration against the workflows you run, not the logo list.


## 6. Adzooma


Adzooma


The free tier is the reason to look at[Adzooma](https://www.adzooma.com/) . It connects Google, Microsoft and Meta advertising accounts, produces PPC performance reports with prioritized opportunities, and handles campaign and budget management with email and Slack alerts.


Read the limits before you build a client process on it. Free reporting is **monthly** , and the free tier limits alerts and users. Scheduled performance reports are labeled **"coming soon"** on the pricing page. Paid tiers give more frequent analysis and additional alerts.


That cadence matters for agencies. A monthly summary can look polished while a purchase tag has been broken since the last release.


Adzooma isn't a dedicated conversion-tracking implementation monitor, and it won't validate your dataLayer or check consent state on server-side events. Use it for account summaries and basic analysis on small budgets. If you're weighing where automation should stop and human review should start, our[PPC automation guide](https://www.trackingplan.com/blog/ppc-automation) sets out that boundary.


## 7. Bïrch


Bïrch


Formerly Revealbot,[Bïrch](https://bir.ch/) is for teams that want rule logic beyond native automated rules. It runs across Meta, Google, TikTok and Snapchat, with custom conditions and timeframes, multiple actions per rule including notifications and campaign changes, external data inputs from sources such as Google Sheets and attribution tools, and bulk creative workflows through the Stage product. A **14-day trial** is available without a credit card.


Rules are where bad data becomes expensive fast. A rule that pauses ad sets below a ROAS threshold acts on the conversion value the platform received, not the value your backend recorded.[Google's enhanced conversions documentation](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/11956168) describes diagnostics for **coverage** (the percentage of eligible conversion events containing sufficient user-provided data), **match rate** , and **conversion uplift** , because hashed customer data determines which conversions get associated with ad interactions at all.


- **Watch before automating:** coverage and match rate on your main actions, then the rule thresholds.
- **Plan limits:** Essential plans don't include the full Pro automation feature set.
- **Review discipline:** dry-run new rules on notifications only for a full week before letting them change live campaigns.


External data triggers help, but they move the trust boundary to your sheet. Someone still owns that feed.


## 8. Madgicx


Madgicx


E-commerce teams running mostly Meta get more from[Madgicx](https://madgicx.com/) than from a search-first tool. It combines Meta-focused automation and audience tools, cross-channel reporting and analytics, and creative and ad-management features, with integrations reaching Google Ads, GA4, TikTok and Shopify. One plan covers automation, targeting, analytics and ad management.


Reporting that pulls GA4 and Meta side by side will show two purchase totals, and the gap usually sits in deduplication, consent state or attribution windows rather than in the campaigns. Seeing the gap in one dashboard doesn't resolve it.


Test fast. The trial runs **seven days** , pricing varies with spend, and pricing details can differ between vendor materials, so confirm the numbers for your spend band in writing.


- **Good fit:** a Shopify brand scaling Meta creative and audiences.
- **Poor fit:** deep Google and Microsoft search auditing.
- **Before day seven:** run your intended workflow end to end, including a real purchase test.


I wouldn't buy it as an Optmyzr replacement for search. I would buy it for paid social creative operations, with measurement checked separately.


## 9. Skai


Skai


Skai is enterprise omnichannel: paid search, paid social and retail media in one platform, with automation and optimization tools, competitive insights and search-term analysis on higher tiers, and enterprise audit, QA and customer-journey capabilities on top tiers. Published annual tiers include dedicated customer success support.


The starting cost rules it out for most small advertisers, and annual pricing with spend bands fits poorly against low-spend accounts. If your main requirement is Google Ads auditing, this is more platform than you need.


For large multi-market programs, the harder question is governance across teams. Most Optmyzr alternatives roundups mention automated reporting, alerts and multi-account support without explaining how a team proves every account's tracking still works after a release or a consent change.


Ask who owns that proof in each region, and how consent evidence is stored for websites and server-side implementations. Then decide whether the platform's QA tier covers it or you need a separate monitoring layer.


## 10. MarinOne


MarinOne


[MarinOne](https://www.marinsoftware.com/) handles campaign operations for mid-market and enterprise advertisers across paid search, paid social, retail media and app advertising. Search and social management sit in one platform, with budget tracking, forecasting and bidding, bulk workflows and automation rules, and reporting that integrates external revenue data. Marin offers product demonstrations and a **30-day trial** , while some tiers require a sales conversation and order-form configuration.


Revenue integration is the feature to scrutinize.[Google's offline conversion import guidance](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/10029210?hl=en) says advertisers should upload conversions **at least daily** , or keep a consistent schedule such as every two days or every week if daily isn't possible, upload all conversions with values when using Target CPA, Target ROAS or Maximize Conversion Value, and keep the data consistent for **one to two conversion cycles** before adding the action to the main Conversions column.


- **Check the schedule:** a missed import day looks like a performance drop to the bidder.
- **Check the values:** revenue feeds that send zero or stale values distort value-based bidding.
- **Check the settings:** primary versus secondary configuration decides whether the import bids at all.


Setup and integrations may need vendor support, and higher-tier pricing isn't fully published. Single-channel teams will carry overhead they don't use.

## Match the tool to the failure you see most


A campaign manager cannot fix a missing conversion signal by changing bids. Start with the failure that costs you the most time or money, and write it in one sentence: “Search terms are wasting budget.” “Client budgets overspend.” “Meta reports twice the purchases our backend does.” These call for different tools: search audits, budget control, or conversion-data checks.


If bids run on the wrong numbers, reconcile the conversion layer first. Compare event definitions, counting rules, attribution windows, consent behavior and imported conversions. Analytics and ad-platform totals are not interchangeable. Then check identity:[Google's enhanced conversions guidance](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/11956168) explains that more match keys increase the probability of matching conversion events, and[its guidance for leads](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/14274408) recommends including GCLIDs with uploaded events whenever possible. Missing click IDs and duplicate order IDs need separate checks and clear owners.


Use the trial to test the failure you need to catch.


- **The job:** Choose bids and budgets, search audits, pacing, cross-channel reporting, or conversion data quality according to the problem.
- **The trial:** Run your real workflow, including checks after a release, rather than judging the demo alone.
- **The pricing model:** Check flat fees, spend-based charges or annual bands, including what happens above the cap.
- **The channels:** Confirm coverage for the networks you use and those you expect to add.


Trackingplan offers a **9-day free trial** and lets visitors explore sample data first. It checks conversion signals across more than 170 analytics and ad providers, including duplicate purchases, click-ID gaps, match rate and UTMs. Daily or weekly tasks can send findings with underlying hits to Slack, Teams, email or a webhook. For the checks to run between audits, see[PPC monitoring](https://www.trackingplan.com/blog/ppc-monitoring) .


For agencies, recurring client checks and attached hits give analysts concrete evidence for client updates and implementation handoffs. Assign each finding to whoever owns the tag or integration. Keep storefront speed work separate from conversion QA:[how Shugert Marketing speeds up stores](https://shugertmarketing.com/services/performance-fix) concerns performance fixes, not PPC monitoring.


If performance conversations keep ending with “the tracking might be off,” resolve that uncertainty before adding more campaign automation. Start the trial at[Trackingplan](https://www.trackingplan.com/) , or use sample data to assess whether the findings support your team's troubleshooting workflow.
